scope: The 39 direct-current-engine MIR1-MIR3 tag-source rows recorded in spec/inventory/migration-origins.json: 19 F200 and 20 F210. This is a bounded Git-object audit of runtime control paths and persistent writers, not an inspection of release archives, source saves, engines, or a migration decoder.
limits: A tag-tree body is not proof that a matching published archive shipped that body. Archive identity, save shape, and source-to-successor applicability remain separately evidenced.
No result here proves a saved-state upgrade, native execution, or that a current MIR5 reader may safely import an observed field.
The seven data-only rows have no root control.lua. Their absent runtime code does not prove that their saves have no migration obligation.
The final-tag literal absence scan is intentionally narrow; it does not establish universal absence of a browser, credit, contribution, or other writer in every earlier tree.

data_only_without_root_control.finding: No root control.lua is present in these tag trees. No runtime writer is inferred from this absence.

writers.semantics: Initializes storage.mir.scripted_techs and dispatches init, configuration, research, effects-reset, and plant-seed handlers.
Captures or rebases the shared spoil-time baseline and applies/restores the MIR multiplier.
Rebuilds a per-force multiplier snapshot and uses it only when handling a planted seed.

writer.semantics: Persists the prototype adoption signature and resets technology effects when that signature changes.

writers.semantics: Registers scripted technologies and settings-profile commands only when their target features are enabled.
Selects the target-declared storage or global backend; it does not itself transform existing state.
Creates backend.mir and named buckets lazily.

writer.semantics: Uses the saved binding units to preserve current-research progress across an adoption signature change.

representative_writer_epochs.semantics: Writes a positive disabled_by_cap marker only after observing technology.enabled and setting it false; it removes queued work above a configured cap and restores only a positive marker.

writer.semantics: Saves the pre-cap visible_when_disabled value independently, restores it only with a positive enablement marker, and records a diagnostic observation.
Records richer adoption binding provenance and retains Factorio-normalized current-research progress rather than applying a second conversion.

For exactly 3.2.0/3.2.1 to 3.2.2 configuration changes, scans researched unlock-space-location effects and calls force.unlock_space_location only for missing current locations. It creates no MIR persistent bucket.

bounded_absence_observation.result: No matching runtime-path literal was found in this final direct F210 tag tree.
bounded_absence_observation.limit: This is not a conclusion about all earlier control bodies and does not establish that current MIR5 browser, native-credit, or spoilage-contribution storage is recoverable from MIR1-MIR3 saves.

reconstructible_from_tag_source_only: Named maximum_level_control policy-v1 buckets and their positive enablement/optional visibility markers
Named scripted-effect and productivity-adoption bucket/field shapes in the stated representative bodies
not_safe_from_tag_source_only: Any source-save value or ownership assertion
Publication/archive identity or native migration success
remaining_recovery_boundary.required_next_evidence: For each selected migration origin, bind a protected source save and actual source archive/engine before admitting a field-specific reader or claiming recovery.
